# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

Platforms/surfaces: iPhone Home/Lock Screen, shared Apple HomeView Modular face, watch glance where appropriate. Data: parcel for Sam at 14 Willow Road, gate code 9182; last server update 35 minutes ago. Widget proposal refreshes every second and puts full address/code on shared face. Delivery lasts 80 minutes. Inline accessory draws Accept, Cancel and Details as independent targets.

name: apple-hig-designing-for-ios
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an iPhone experience for handheld touch, interrupted use, orientation changes, and system entrypoints.

# Make the iPhone task usable in the hand

Read [Designing for iOS](../../references/designing-for-ios.md). Inspect the current task, its entry and return points, supported orientations, input, and any supplied implementation. Distinguish a brief check from extended work. For a review, anchor problems to supplied screens/behavior; for design or adaptation, revise the requested artifact in its existing stack.

Choose what must remain immediately visible during the task. A brief check needs its result and primary action close together; extended editing can expose additional controls without crowding the initial screen. Put frequent touch actions within comfortable reach, generally toward the middle/lower display, while preserving system navigation and swipe-back behavior. Move secondary commands into a short discoverable path rather than shrinking every control to fit.

Trace interruption and resumption: preserve the selected item, draft, or playback context when another app takes focus. Specify portrait/landscape and enlarged-text rearrangements without inventing a new navigation hierarchy for each orientation. Use touch and onscreen keyboard as the baseline, then offer appropriate voice or accessory paths. Add location, biometric, payment, or motion features only when their benefit reduces task effort and access is appropriate.

For repeated out-of-app actions, choose a relevant system entrypoint and a precise destination: a quick action starts an action, search opens the found content, and a widget exposes a useful glance. Do not add every entrypoint to every app.

**Before → decision → after:** A parcel app opens a dense desktop-style table and requires opening three menus to find the latest delivery. A handheld glance needs delivery state first. The revised home screen shows the active parcel and “Show pickup code,” keeps history one step away, and returns a widget tap to that parcel rather than a generic home screen.

Deliver a revised screen/flow or implementation plus interruption, orientation, and text-size acceptance checks. Fail if the primary action becomes unreachable, Back conflicts with a custom gesture, or resuming loses work. Screenshot review cannot establish touch comfort or actual system integration; state pending device checks.

For detailed adaptation use [Layout](../../../apple-hig-foundations/.topics/apple-hig-layout/SKILL.md); for custom touch gestures use [Gestures](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-gestures/SKILL.md); for a chosen glance use [Widgets](../../../apple-hig-system-experiences/.topics/apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md).

name: apple-hig-designing-for-watchos
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting an Apple Watch experience for brief glances, focused actions, complications, wrist-down states, and independence from iPhone.
---

# Fit the task to a wrist glance

Read [Designing for watchOS](../../references/designing-for-watchos.md). Inspect the proposed Watch task, frequency, urgency, companion-phone dependency, and supplied screens. Identify the information needed at wrist raise and the action worth performing there. Choose design, review, or adaptation mode; produce the requested revised artifact rather than transplanting the whole phone app.

Separate a glance from deeper interaction. Put the useful value and next action on one screen when possible, keeping navigation shallow and gestures few. Use the Digital Crown for vertical movement rather than requiring repeated precise swipes. If a task needs prolonged text entry or broad comparisons, simplify its Watch responsibility and provide a coherent continuation elsewhere without making the entire Watch app merely a remote notice.

Choose entrypoints by purpose: a complication supplies recurring glance value and opens the corresponding context; a timely notification should let people act without launching; an Action button suits an essential action useful without looking. Do not require sensor access just because the device provides sensors. Personalize only with an explained task benefit and appropriate permission.

Design wrist-up and Always On information together, including what remains useful and what should become less prominent. Provide independently useful app detail beyond the complication or notification. Preserve progress when the wrist lowers or an interruption occurs.

**Worked transformation:** Before, a tea timer copies a phone recipe browser and requires four screens before starting. Decision: the wrist task is checking and controlling the current steep. After, the first screen shows remaining time and a large Pause/Resume action; Crown navigation reaches saved presets, and a complication opens the running timer directly. The phone retains detailed recipe editing.

Deliver a glance/action flow, entrypoint destinations, and wrist-state behavior or implementation. Fail if a complication opens unrelated content, a routine action requires deep navigation, or lowering the wrist loses the timer. State whether actual Watch readability, Crown response, notification handling, and sensor access were tested; static evidence cannot prove them.

Continue with [Digital Crown](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-digital-crown/SKILL.md), [Always On](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-always-on/SKILL.md), or [Action button](../../../apple-hig-inputs/.topics/apple-hig-action-button/SKILL.md) only for the selected interaction.

name: apple-hig-widgets
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting widgets across families, surfaces, rendering modes, freshness policies, and focused interactions.

# Build a widget around one useful glance

Read [the widgets guide](../../references/widgets.md), including the context/rendering tables relevant to the requested destination. The procedure and example below are application advice; use the guide for supported families, dimensions, and platform facts. Do not turn a reference size into a universal fixed production canvas.

## Establish purpose and destination

Inspect the supplied app, widget design/code, data model, or brief. Determine create, review, or adaptation mode, target OS/surface, widget family, useful changing information, sensitivity, and the app destination after activation. If no family or surface is given, choose the smallest supported one that communicates the requested purpose, state the assumption, and design that concrete variant.

Write the glance question the widget answers. Reject a static app-icon replica or a compressed app dashboard as the purpose. Decide what the person needs immediately, what appears on closer inspection, and what belongs in the app. Record source update frequency separately from system refresh opportunity; neither a design mockup nor an API response proves continuous widget updates.

## Produce a surface-specific contract

1. Choose family and content hierarchy together. A small variant should carry a clear fact or focused action; larger variants add useful information under the same core purpose instead of stretching the small layout. Consult the supported-context tables before proposing variants: tvOS does not support widgets, and accessory, system, and spatial-only families are not interchangeable. Keep specification tables in the reference rather than copying them into the deliverable.
2. Define data behavior: configuration or useful automatic content, realistic preview, initial placeholder, signed-out explanation when sign-in is required, available data during refresh, and stale/unavailable content. Specify freshness wording when age changes the interpretation. Match timeline requests to meaningful changes and expected viewing; use system date/time presentation for changing time where applicable. Keep useful existing data visible while refreshing. If the requested value requires frequent updates for a bounded event, load live-activities instead of promising a constantly refreshing widget.
3. Map interactions to outcomes. Ordinary activation opens the relevant app content; native buttons/toggles may perform simple relevant actions in place. Give separate targets distinguishable purposes and deep-link precisely. Inline accessories have one tap target, so collapse competing controls into one useful destination rather than drawing fake independent buttons. Do not recreate navigation, forms, or a miniature app inside the widget.
4. Design required rendering variants rather than relying on brand color. Establish primary versus accent hierarchy for accented mode and meaningful grayscale emphasis for vibrant mode. Preserve labels, symbols, or shapes that carry state when color disappears. Check light/dark, tint/clear, background removal, and low-light/Always On variants only where that surface uses them. The source table excludes accented Mac support while prose conflicts; disclose the inconsistency and verify current official support before promising it. Do not resolve it by inventing a capability.
5. Make layout flexible: system text styles and actual text, adaptable margins, container-relative corner shapes, and assets that remain useful when scaled. Use the reference's size guidance for the selected context, including iPad canvas-versus-device scaling. Review accessibility text sizes for supported platforms and ensure reduced detail preserves the glance question, rather than simply shrinking every element.
6. Apply the destination's consequential branch. For StandBy/CarPlay, prioritize large glanceable information, removable backgrounds, and low-light StandBy red monochrome. For a shared HomeView Modular face, assess whose information becomes visible to the household and choose a safe summary/configuration. For watch Smart Stack, prioritize relevance and a legible compact hierarchy. For visionOS, specify near/default and distant simplified content, surface/mounting suitability, frame/treatment choice, palette/lighting variants, and scale range; distant views enlarge key information and remove controls. Recessed-only mounting cannot support horizontal placement, and frame-width choices cannot be repaired with layout adaptation after selection.

Perform the authorized work: implement the widget in the supplied stack when requested, produce an annotated variant/state specification for design, or report evidence-backed defects with concrete replacements for review. For adaptation, retain the glance question while changing family, hierarchy, interactions, and appearance for the destination.

## Deliver and verify

Deliver the changed artifact with a compact variant contract: purpose; surface/family; primary content; freshness/stale policy; configuration/auth state; tap/in-place-action destinations; rendering variants; and destination-specific checks. Include realistic example data and mark simulated data as simulated. A review must identify the affected variant and observed evidence, not merely repeat best practices.

Verify that each variant answers its glance question with long/localized text, realistic edge values, and relevant accessibility sizes. Follow each tap and in-place action to its intended object; confirm rendering changes preserve meaning when color/background disappears. Check stale content cannot masquerade as live data and previews accurately represent the chosen variants. Fail the design for unsupported family/surface claims, unbounded refresh promises, sensitive shared content without a deliberate policy, unreadable tinted hierarchy, or separate inline tap targets. Distinguish static inspection from timeline/runtime, VoiceOver, spatial distance/lighting, device rendering, and household behavior tests; do not claim these were run on a Linux host.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** A reading app proposes one stretched widget for phone Home Screen and Lock Screen. It shows six book covers, a red “overdue” dot, and three tiny controls; the brief promises second-by-second updates.

**Decision:** The useful glance is “What am I reading next?” Home Screen and accessory contexts need different hierarchies. Reading progress can refresh meaningfully without a continuous timer, and overdue status must survive desaturation.

**After:** A small Home Screen variant shows the current book title, progress text, and a precise open-book destination; a larger variant adds the next queued book under the same purpose. An inline Lock Screen variant reads `Continue: The Orchard` with one destination. Replace the color-only dot with `Due tomorrow` where relevant, retain last known progress during refresh, and preview believable data. Verify tint/grayscale legibility and deep links; label refresh timing as system-controlled. This is a proposed design, not measured behavior of a real app.

## Conditional handoffs

Use live-activities for bounded frequently updated events; complications for watch-face-specific placement; controls for a system control rather than informational widget; layout for unresolved adaptive geometry; and accessibility for reading order or contrast failures. Carry the variant contract forward so related work preserves the original glance purpose.

# Give the live event a start and an end

# Make the task accessible

Read [Accessibility guidance](../../references/accessibility.md) before applying platform values. This procedure turns that guidance into task-level changes; its artifact format and prioritization are application engineering advice, not additional Apple requirements.

## Establish what can be evaluated

Identify the supported platform, the person's task from entry to completion, and whether the request is design, review, or adaptation. Inspect the supplied screens, content, interaction description, semantics, or implementation. Record which evidence exists: a screenshot can establish visible labels and geometry, but cannot establish spoken names, focus order, alternative activation, or preference behavior. Continue using explicit assumptions when the platform or behavior is missing; ask only when the choice changes the requested result.

For a review, connect each finding to an observed barrier and its consequence for that task. Separate untested behavior needing verification from confirmed defects. For a design or adaptation, change the authorized artifact itself: a revised screen specification, interaction contract, or implementation. A general accessibility checklist alone is not the deliverable.

## Remove the barriers that the task contains

Trace the task without assuming sight, hearing, fine motor control, speech, or fast responses. Select the applicable branches:

- **Reading and visual distinctions:** Preserve content and available actions when text enlarges. Use the guide's platform-specific text defaults and minima; its resizing guidance is at least 200%, with 140% stated for watchOS. Reflow or expose another usable arrangement rather than clipping essential labels. Pair color distinctions with text, shape, or symbols. Evaluate actual foreground/background combinations in light and dark appearances; use a contrast calculator and preserve the guide's stated contrast-table scope instead of claiming that its values alone establish conformance. If the default scheme falls short, specify the Increase Contrast treatment.
- **Information carried by sound or imagery:** Identify what information would disappear when sound or sight is unavailable. Choose captions for synchronized audible events, subtitles for dialogue translation, audio description for visual events, or transcripts for a complete text account according to the content. Specify descriptions for meaningful interface/content imagery and omit redundant decoration. Pair essential sound feedback with a perceivable visual or appropriate haptic equivalent.
- **Manipulation and navigation:** Distinguish visible control size from its actual activation area and separation. Use the guide's platform default as the starting point; its smaller minimum is not a blanket recommendation for dense controls. Replace essential complex or repeated gestures with a labeled onscreen action. Make the complete task navigable and activatable with the supported keyboard and assistive input paths; speech must not be necessary. Preserve system accessibility shortcuts. For custom controls, specify names, roles, values, states, and task order rather than assuming their appearance supplies semantics.
- **Time, motion, and comprehension:** Give people time to read and act; prefer explicit dismissal when transient content requires attention. If motion is present, define a Reduce Motion version that retains state and meaning while reducing automatic movement, bounce, zoom, or depth changes. If media autoplays, provide playback control and consider a global preference; honor Dim Flashing Lights where applicable. Keep the task's navigation and wording consistent rather than adding instructional clutter.

Apply the relevant platform condition. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks with one interaction per screen and the source's two confirmations for difficult-to-reverse actions in that mode. For visionOS, keep controls in comfortable view, avoid head-locked content and repeated large gestures, and accommodate hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. These conditions do not apply automatically to every platform.

## Deliver and check the result

Return the revised artifact or evidence-based review, including the barrier, the concrete change, and its acceptance check. State which platform/preferences were considered and which claims remain unverified. Prioritize blockers to completing the task over cosmetic refinements.

Exercise each selected alternative along the same entry-to-completion path. Fail the check if essential content or actions disappear at the specified text scale, information remains available through only one sense, a required gesture has no equivalent, focus cannot reach/activate a necessary control, or a requested motion accommodation removes meaning. Measure contrast and activation geometry when the evidence permits; report missing measurements rather than inventing them. Use Accessibility Inspector and relevant VoiceOver, Switch Control, Full Keyboard Access, AssistiveTouch, or Pointer Control tests on supported Apple environments. Static inspection or a Linux run cannot establish those runtime results, Apple-device comfort, or App Store Accessibility Nutrition Label eligibility.

## Worked transformation

**Before:** An iPad astronomy log marks observation quality only with green/red dots, announces saving with a chime, and exposes Delete only by a two-finger gesture.

**Decision:** Logging must remain understandable without color or sound and operable without that gesture. Retain compact rows while making status and actions explicit.

**After:** Each row reads “Clear” or “Clouded” alongside its symbol; saving exposes a persistent “Saved” state; a labeled row action opens Delete. The screen specification includes expanded-text reflow, semantic row status, and keyboard/assistive activation acceptance checks. These are proposed changes until the actual implementation passes those checks; the specification does not claim VoiceOver was tested.

## Continue only where needed

For detailed spoken structure and rotor navigation, use [VoiceOver](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-voiceover/SKILL.md). For text reflow/type choices use [Typography](../apple-hig-typography/SKILL.md); for a motion accommodation use [Motion](../apple-hig-motion/SKILL.md). If spatial comfort dominates the task, use [Spatial layout](../apple-hig-spatial-layout/SKILL.md). Keep the task's accessibility acceptance checks when handing off.

# Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. End immediately when the task ends: Dynamic Island/CarPlay remove it, while Lock Screen, Mac, and watch can retain it for up to 4 hours. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; # Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

Build an interface people can understand, perceive through different senses, and adapt to their preferred methods. Treat accessibility as a design input and audit with Accessibility Inspector. Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. # Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. End immediately when the task ends: Dynamic Island/CarPlay remove it, while Lock Screen, Mac, and watch can retain it for up to 4 hours. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped. Without a container background, bold can improve visibility; do not rely on unpredictable cast shadows. # Pickup summary and delivery Live Activity

Design specification based on "'`interface.md` and the installed local HIG snapshot (2026-10-25). No web access, SDK verification, implementation, simulator, GUI, device, or assistive-technology execution was performed. Official links below identify the local guidance'"'s sources; they were not opened.

## Decisions and supplied evidence

The task is a brief household pickup check plus private tracking of one bounded, 80-minute delivery. The brief supplies one parcel, a recipient, a full address and gate credential, and a server update aged 35 minutes. It supplies no confirmed pickup readiness, delivery stage, ETA, timestamp, backend contract, or minimum OS version. Do not invent these values. Examples below that describe readiness or transit are conditional fixtures.

Replace the proposed one-second widget reload loop with meaningful timeline entries and system-controlled refresh opportunities. Use a Live Activity for frequent changes during the delivery. Replace the inline Accept/Cancel/Details targets with one parcel-details destination. Exclude recipient, address and gate code from household content. These correct the supplied proposal against [Widgets: Updating widget content, Adding interactivity, Apple HomeView](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets).

## Household pickup widget

Glance question: “Is there a household pickup to check, and how trustworthy is this summary?”

Use a separate **Household pickups** configuration with a strict safe-data projection. An authorized person selects a household and explicitly enables sharing: “Show pickup counts and status to everyone in this household. Names, addresses, and access codes stay private.” Default before setup: "'`Choose household in app`. Only parcels explicitly shared with that household contribute. Do not automatically publish Sam'"'s parcel merely because it exists on a connected phone. The shared Modular face is household-visible, distinct from personalized Home Screens; use system-small there, not a watch complication. [Widgets: Apple HomeView](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Apple-HomeView).

| Surface/family | Content, highest priority first | Activation |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone Home Screen, system small | "'`Household pickups`; safe count/status; freshness | Entire widget opens that household'"'s pickup list |
| Shared HomeView Modular, system small | Same safe summary, enlarged status, removable background | Opens safe household pickup context where supported; private details require personal authenticated continuation |
| iPhone Lock Screen, accessory rectangular | "'`Pickup status`; safe status/count; freshness | One household pickup-list destination |
| iPhone Lock Screen, accessory inline | `Pickups: update needed` for supplied stale fixture; fresh conditional fixture `Pickups: 1 ready` | One target only; no button-like Accept/Cancel/Details regions |
| Optional Watch face, accessory rectangular | Same safe status plus age; native face typography | Opens Watch household pickup view |

Do not offer medium/large widgets until additional useful household summary information exists. Do not claim accessory families work on the shared Modular surface. Watch support assumes a native companion view; otherwise defer the optional complication. A complication is watchOS-specific, while iPhone Lock Screen accessories are widgets. [Complications: Best practices and Platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/complications).

Concrete supplied-data layout, only after sharing is authorized:

```text
Household pickups
1 parcel to check
Update needed
Last updated 35 min ago
```

Count describes the cached shared record; it does not imply readiness. If not shared, show `No shared pickups` only after a successful authorized query confirms that result. A fresh confirmed ready fixture may read `1 pickup ready · Updated 2 min ago`. Do not display “ready” from an unknown stage.

Gallery description: `Check household pickups.` Use simulated, labeled example content without personal data. Initial placeholder preserves title and redacted status blocks, never fabricated counts. Signed out: `Sign in to view pickups`; revoked membership: `Household unavailable`; confirmed empty result: `No pickups`; failed first load: `Pickup status unavailable`. Each opens the relevant setup, sign-in, or household context. Never equate missing data with zero pickups.

## Freshness and offline contract

These thresholds are product decisions for validation with operations, not Apple requirements. Keep event time, last successful server confirmation, and local fetch time separate. Re-rendering cached data never renews server freshness.

| State | Entry condition | Widget / expanded activity behavior |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh | Valid server confirmation age ≤5 min | Confirmed state; `Updated … ago`; ETA only if separately valid |
| Stale | Age >5 min or ETA validity expires | `Update needed`; keep explicitly last-known state and timestamp; suppress current ETA/countdown |
| Offline with cache | Observed connectivity/fetch evidence, not just old data | `Offline · Last updated … ago`; cached status labeled last known |
| Failed/unknown connection | Fetch failure without proof of offline status | `Couldn'"'t update"'`; timestamp; no invented offline assertion |
| Refreshing | Fetch in progress | Keep existing safe content and freshness; no full skeleton replacement |
| No cache | No valid snapshot | `Status unavailable`; open app to retry |

The supplied 35-minute age is stale. Connectivity is unknown. It must not show “live,” a current ETA, or “offline” solely from that age. Compact forms prioritize `Update needed` over a count if both will not fit; full timestamp remains in the destination. At very large text, use `Update needed` plus a compact age rather than dropping the freshness warning.

Request widget timelines at meaningful status/window changes and the five-minute freshness boundary; request reload after relevant server changes when supported. System scheduling can delay rendering: keep last-updated text visible even in the fresh template so an old entry cannot silently look current. Use system relative date presentation where supported, never per-second network polling. The authenticated app retries on opening and offers explicit retry; reconnect alone does not mark data fresh. Only a newer valid response clears stale/offline. Reject older/out-of-order event revisions. [Widgets: Updating widget content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content).

## Private delivery Live Activity

“Private” means a personal delivery context with minimized public-facing content, not a guarantee that a Lock Screen or paired display is visible only to its owner. Never put Sam'"'s name, the full address, gate code, a route map, or credential-bearing links in activity content, previews, spoken labels, or payloads. All surface layouts use generic "'`Delivery`; sensitive detail is available only after app authentication and parcel authorization. Even the unlocked activity omits the gate code. This is a deliberate stricter product policy based on [Live Activities: Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices) and [Privacy: Protecting data](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Protecting-data).

Start once after server-confirmed dispatch for this delivery, when expected by the person, subject to system authorization. Offer `Track delivery` in the parcel view and an easy per-delivery opt-out. If unavailable or declined, the app'"'s delivery view remains usable. Do not start a live event from the 35-minute-old record alone. Track one activity per delivery; update the existing activity across its stages.

| Presentation | Fresh confirmed transit fixture | Stale/offline adaptation |
|---|---|---|
| Compact leading / trailing | Parcel-transit symbol / valid estimated minutes such as "'`20m`, otherwise short stage | Parcel-warning symbol / `Stale`; use offline symbol only with evidence |
| Minimal, including competing activities | Parcel symbol with small transit state mark; completion check only when confirmed | Parcel plus warning mark; meaningful status, not static logo |
| Expanded | `Delivery`; `On the way`; `Estimated 14:20–14:30` only if provided and valid; `Updated 2 min ago` | `Delivery · Update needed`; `Last known: On the way`; `Last updated 35 min ago`; omit ETA |
| Lock Screen | Same hierarchy in a distinct delivery layout | Same last-known labeling and age; no sensitive identity |
| StandBy | Scaled Lock Screen layout with less secondary detail | Large freshness warning retained; red Night Mode legible |
| Watch Smart Stack | Stage and freshness, combining compact content or custom small layout | Warning replaces ETA; tap opens native delivery context if available, otherwise system paired-phone continuation |

Both compact halves and the activity body open the same opaque delivery-ID route. Authentication resumes that exact delivery; wrong-account access shows an unavailable state. No sensitive values in the URL. Retain parcel identity and stage positions as the activity expands. Use system-controlled Dynamic Island backgrounds; custom background only on Lock Screen. Fit limited-width content within the guide'"'s 28-pt circle guidance, with no fixed universal canvas. [Live Activities: Presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation).

Use a single details destination; there is no necessary direct mutation for this glance. Accept and Cancel remain authenticated in-app workflows. An offline request must not display success without server confirmation. No fake independent inline targets and no claim that tapping bypasses locking. A future essential direct action would need its own authorization, pending/failure, and retry contract.

### Lifecycle and updates

"'`Not started → dispatched → on the way → arriving → delivered/cancelled/failed` uses authoritative server events. Freshness/connection state overlays any nonterminal stage. Do not infer completion from the planned duration, elapsed-time percentage, or ETA reaching zero.

The expected event lasts 80 minutes, within the local HIG'"'s preference for bounded events ideally no more than eight hours. At start, assign a product tracking cutoff of dispatch +120 minutes (80 minutes plus a proposed 40-minute grace period). If no terminal confirmation arrives, end tracking with "'`Tracking ended · Check delivery status`; the delivery itself remains unresolved in the app. Do not auto-restart indefinitely. An authenticated fresh confirmation can offer a new explicitly bounded tracking session if needed. This cutoff is a product proposal requiring operational approval, not a platform limit.

On delivered/cancelled/failed confirmation, end immediately; remove from Dynamic Island and other nonretaining destinations. Retain a safe Lock Screen summary for 15 minutes where supported, then dismiss. Use `Delivered`, `Delivery cancelled`, or `Delivery needs attention` accurately. Persist the result in the app for later reading. Stopping tracking or system dismissal does not cancel delivery. At cutoff without connectivity, end using the planned deadline where supported; actual background enforcement is an implementation acceptance gate.

Send updates only when content changes, with freshness expiry scheduled independently of network updates. Alert only for confirmed arrival requiring attention or a blocking exception; do not send a duplicate push for the same update. Routine progress and stale state remain quiet. Foreground and remote updates share revision ordering; terminal events close the activity and reject later nonterminal updates. Verify ActivityKit lifecycle, expiry and termination scheduling against the eventual SDK; no API availability is established by this design. [Live Activities: Starting, updating, and ending](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity).

Where the system propagates the activity, CarPlay must remain useful with controls disabled; paired Mac activation uses iPhone Mirroring. Do not promise Live Activities on tvOS or visionOS. No custom driving workflow is required. HomeView receives only the separate safe pickup widget, not private delivery content.

## Data, appearance and access

| Data | Purpose and exposure |
|---|---|
| Household ID, shared safe count/status, confirmation timestamp | Authorized household summary projection; revoke access and clear cached projection on membership/account changes |
| Opaque delivery ID, stage, revision, timestamps, valid ETA window, tracking deadline | Personal activity projection; no personal destination or access credential |
| Recipient/address | Authenticated parcel detail only, authorized per account |
| Gate credential | Explicit reveal in authenticated parcel detail only; established protected storage, no widget/activity cache or logs |

No new location, contacts, HomeKit, or tracking permission is needed merely to display server-provided logistics status. Sharing setup is an ordinary product choice, not a simulated system permission prompt. Revalidate disclosure requirements against actual storage/transfer behavior. Revocation must clear projections locally and propagate removal where possible; offline remote displays may retain old safe summaries until refreshed, so privacy relies on payload minimization rather than immediate remote erasure. [Privacy: Best practices and Requesting permission](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy).

Use semantic system type: headline for status, body for stage, caption for freshness, medium or stronger for activity status. Actual text and scalable symbols, no rasterized labels. Stack age beneath stage at enlarged sizes; drop decorative identity before status/freshness. Preserve the glance question through widget Large–AX5, iOS text enlargement of at least 200%, and watchOS at least 140%; fixed accessories use concise safe text with full detail in the accessible destination. These are design targets pending fit checks. [Typography: Supporting Dynamic Type](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#Supporting-Dynamic-Type), [Accessibility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility).

Full color uses semantic light/dark foregrounds. Accented mode keeps status primary and supporting symbol accent. Vibrant mode uses grayscale luminance hierarchy, not white-opacity tricks. Text plus warning/check symbols preserves meaning in tint, clear, grayscale and red Night Mode. HomeView/StandBy backgrounds are removable. Always On keeps the same safe fields and positions, dims secondary information, retains freshness, and uses no continuous animation; waking restores the same delivery context. Device support must be verified; the local Always On guide names particular iPhone Pro models rather than all iPhones. [Widgets: Rendering modes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Rendering-modes), [Always On](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/always-on).

Accessibility contract: expose status, freshness and destination as meaningful text; decorative parcel art adds no redundant announcement. A combined widget label could read `Household pickups. One parcel to check. Update needed. Last updated 35 minutes ago.` Never include private data in accessibility labels. Use native link behavior for the single destination. In-app controls use comfortable 44×44-pt default activation areas on iOS/watchOS. No essential information depends on color, sound or animation. Runtime spoken order and activation remain unverified.

## Acceptance checks and evidence still missing

**Passed — static specification inspection only:** supplied 35-minute fixture is stale without an invented offline claim; household projection omits personal identity and credentials; inline accessory has one destination; widget scheduling makes no continuous refresh promise; delivery has explicit start, terminal signals, fallback cutoff and retention; no ETA or pickup readiness is invented from the brief. Installed root, selected families, topic procedures and supporting local guides were read through separate file-reading commands.

**Failed — supplied proposal:** per-second widget refresh promise; full address/code on the shared face; three independent inline targets. This specification replaces each. No implemented product was inspected, so these are proposal findings, not measured runtime defects.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

| Scenario | Required result / missing evidence |
|---|---|
| Inject age 4:59 → 5:01 → 35 min; delay reload; fail fetch; reconnect | Freshness warning/age remains truthful; no stale ETA; offline only with evidence; newer server confirmation alone restores freshness. Needs timeline and network execution. |
| Dispatch, arrival, terminal event, cutoff with no network, late reordered update | One activity, no inferred delivery, prompt ending, 15-minute summary expiry, no resurrection or duplicate alert. Needs backend event contract and ActivityKit execution. |
| Shared/nonshared parcel; revoke membership; sign out; wrong account; locked tap | Only approved summary visible; private route authenticates and preserves destination; no secret in payload, cache, link, log, preview or spoken output. Needs data-flow/security inspection and locked-device tests. |
| Tap every surface; inline boundaries; two or more simultaneous activities | Correct household/delivery route, single inline target, informative minimal state. Needs native navigation/system integration tests. |
| Smallest/largest supported iPhone and Watch; long localized strings; text sizes through AX5/Bold Text | Status and freshness remain legible without overlap; companion app exposes full detail. Needs previews, actual rendered geometry and device-distance checks. |
| Light/dark, tinted/clear, vibrant grayscale, removed background, red Night Mode, Always On/wrist lower | Meaning survives loss of color/background; no sensitive reveal or layout jump; contrast measured with actual foreground/background. Needs rendered variants, measurements and supported devices. |
| VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, relevant keyboard/assistive paths | Meaningful labels, no hidden secrets or fake controls, destination reachable and activatable. Needs Accessibility Inspector and assistive-technology execution. |
| Watch/StandBy/CarPlay/paired Mac propagation | Readable glance, disabled driving controls harmless, correct paired continuation. Needs supported hardware/OS and simulator evidence. |

Still missing: minimum OS and hardware list; SDK/API feasibility for household/remote surfaces, expiry and background cutoff; genuine pickup stage and time data; service freshness/ETA guarantees; validated sharing and authorization model; user confirmation of the proposed five-minute stale and 120-minute tracking thresholds; household comprehension and privacy research. The local snapshot contains unrelated Mac accented-mode and legacy complication sizing inconsistencies; this design makes no support or fixed-art sizing promises from those passages. No native rendering, energy, push reliability, accessibility conformance, or platform support certification is claimed.
EOF'
